Dreamerror2026-09-04
Three shell commands hit the hardline blocklist this week: for-loops in a single terminal call exceed the parser limit
The Hermes gateway has a command parser limit that blocks oversized shell payloads. Three times this week the agent constructed a single terminal command with an inline for-loop (e.g. "for f in ...; do wc -l; done") that exceeded the limit and was hardline-blocked. Each block wastes a full turn - the agent has to retry with a different approach. The trigger is always the same: iterating over multiple files or checking multiple CLI tools in one monolithic command. The fix is behavioural: when iterating, use separate terminal calls or write a temp script first. Not a code change - a pattern the agent should recognise and avoid.
A$1/mo5 min/mo
Why we're suggesting this (3)
  • 30 Aug: "wc -l ... && for f in ~/hermes-deploy-kit/core/learnings/cards/..." blocked as hardline (parser limit)
  • 2 Sep: same pattern with "wc -l core/learnings/catalogue.md && for f in core/learnings/cards/..." blocked again
  • 3 Sep: "for c in claude codex opencode gemini jq; do command -v ..." blocked - checking for installed CLIs in a for-loop
Dreamworkflow2026-09-01
Harvest time-tracking integration lives in ad-hoc /tmp scripts - 15+ write-and-run cycles this week
The Harvest-to-Atlas time-tracking pipeline is being built on the fly, every time. In the last 7 days the agent wrote and ran at least six different /tmp/harvest_*.py scripts - harvest_push_atlas.py, harvest_atlas_note.py, harvest_atlas_learnings.py, harvest_push.py, harvest_push2.py, harvest_extract.py - each requiring a write_file followed by a terminal run, often with environment-variable sourcing preamble repeated verbatim. That is 15+ tool calls that could collapse to a single skill invocation. The scripts are iterative because the integration is young, but the scaffolding pattern is stable. Capture the current best path in a proper skill at skills/snowark/harvest-atlas/ so the next run does not re-derive the approach from scratch. Even a thin SKILL.md with the canonical env-sourcing snippet and the three most-used script templates would cut the cycle in half.
mkdir -p ~/.hermes/skills/snowark/harvest-atlas/scripts
A$5/mo30 min/mo
Why we're suggesting this (3)
  • dream.py repeat candidates show write_file and terminal runs on /tmp/harvest_push_atlas.py (3+2), harvest_atlas_note.py (3+3), harvest_atlas_learnings.py (3+2), harvest_push.py (2), harvest_push2.py (2), harvest_extract.py (2) - 15+ total cycles
  • Each cycle follows the same pattern: write_file to /tmp then terminal run with source ~/.hermes/.env preamble
  • No harvest-atlas skill exists in the skills/ inventory - the pattern is entirely ad-hoc each time
Dreamworkflow2026-09-04
Inline Asana and Google API calls are back: 32 hand-rolled urllib calls this week despite the asana-api skill consolidation
The asana-api skill was consolidated on 19 August and the dream-wf-inline-api-calls recommendation was marked complete, but 32 terminal commands this week still inline Python with urllib.request to call Asana or Google APIs directly. Most follow the pattern "source .env && python3 -c import os,json,urllib.request". The consolidated skill covers task creation and comments, but the agent falls back to inline code for sections lookups, tag operations, attachment uploads, and bulk queries. The fix is to audit the remaining inline patterns against the skill, wrap the top 5 missing operations as helper functions in the asana-api skill, and add a trigger to the skill that catches the urllib.request pattern.
cd ~/.hermes && grep -c urllib.request logs/tool-calls.jsonl
A$3/mo10 min/mo

  • 18 terminal commands matching "source .env && python3 -c import os, json, urllib.request pat = os.environ" in the 7-day tool-call window - all inline Asana/Google API calls
  • 14 additional terminal commands with the same urllib.request + .env sourcing pattern (variant with cd ~/.hermes prefix) - total 32 inline API calls
